items.title: Youth engagement before enforcement part of police plan for Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Police plan to engage youth in Mississauga and Brampton Peel Regional Police are working on a new plan aimed at improving how it connects with young people, and the public is being asked to help shape it. The Youth Engagement Plan developed by the Peel Police Service Board is intended to strengthen positive relationships between police and young people across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, including students, educators, school communities and organizations that work with youth. The plan is still being developed, and the board says hearing directly from the community will be an important part of the process. “Meaningful youth engagement begins with meaningful community engagement,” said Sumeeta Kohli, chair of the board’s Governance and Human Rights Committee. The board is particularly looking to hear from students, parents, educators, community organizations and other residents about their experiences and perspectives. READ MORE: Peel police anti-racism plan brings independent oversight to Mississauga, Brampton The effort comes as police services across the country increasingly look at how they can build trust and positive relationships with young people before interactions with police become focused on enforcement.

items.title: Well-known restaurant forced to close after failing health inspection in Mississauga
items.summary: A restaurant in Brampton has been shut down by Peel Public Health after a failed health inspection. Swagruhas, located at 2970 Drew Rd, was inspected and closed on Thursday, Sept. 3. The South Indian vegetarian restaurant specializes in sweet and savoury dosas. Peel Public Health’s report states that the restaurant did not properly store food to prevent contamination and/or adulteration and did not take adequate measures to prevent pests, as well as various other health violations. The restaurant is closed until further notice and may reopen after passing a follow-up inspection. This is the only failed inspection on file for this restaurant, which has inspections going back to October 2024. Peel Public Health regularly inspects restaurants in the region, issuing a green card if the inspection is passed, a yellow card for a conditional pass (minor infractions), and a red card if significant health risks are found. A restaurant that’s issued a red card is forced to close until it can pass a follow-up inspection.

items.title: Toronto Pearson to Offer First Nonstop Flights to Norway Under Air Canada's 2027 Expansion
items.summary: According to INsauga, Air Canada has announced three new international routes launching from Toronto Pearson International Airport in Mississauga in the summer of 2027, including its first nonstop flights to Norway. The outlet reports the new destinations are Oslo, Shannon in Ireland, and Nice in France, with Oslo becoming Air Canada's third Scandinavian route alongside existing service to Stockholm and Copenhagen. INsauga reports the Oslo flights will fly aboard the airline's new Airbus A321XLR aircraft, which features a premium Signature cabin with lie-flat seats. According to the outlet, Toronto Pearson president and CEO Deborah Flint said the new routes strengthen links to global markets and give passengers more choice. INsauga reports the airline is also adding a seasonal Toronto to London-Heathrow day-tripper service, daily flights to Shanghai, and a new year-round route to Guatemala City starting this December.

items.title: Province of Ontario's Name Traces Directly Back to Lake Ontario, Column Explains
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, a recent column traces the centuries-old history behind the name Lake Ontario, noting that the Province of Ontario itself takes its name directly from the lake. The outlet writes that the lake's shores have been home to Indigenous peoples for thousands of years before European colonization. Modern Mississauga Media reports that after 1608 the region was part of New France's Pays d'en Haut, or Upper Country. According to the outlet, Britain reorganized the area as the Province of Quebec following the 1763 Treaty of Paris, which ended French colonial rule after the fall of New France. Modern Mississauga Media reports the Constitutional Act of 1791 later split that territory into Upper Canada, now Ontario, and Lower Canada, now Quebec. The column was prompted partly by recent attention in the United States over proposals to rename the lake, which the outlet says has only reinforced pride in the name's Canadian identity.

items.title: Road safety crucial as kids go back to school in Mississauga: city
items.summary: Drivers and others are being reminded about road safety as neighbourhood streets in Mississauga are about to get much busier with young pedestrians, school buses and parents dropping off and picking up their kids. Early next week, tens of thousands of students will return to classes in Mississauga for the 2026-27 school year. Both the City of Mississauga and Peel Regional Police have similar messages for drivers as they travel in and near the many school zones across the city — slow down, watch for kids both on foot and on bicycles, and obey school bus signals and all traffic signs. “In the coming days, school zones, crossings and neighbourhood streets will become noticeably busier. The city is reminding drivers, transit users, cyclists, e-scooter users and pedestrians to be extra careful during the busy morning and afternoon school rush,” city officials said in an online reminder to the community on Thursday. “With increased traffic and activity on the road, the risk of collisions is higher. ” City officials and police note that streets, driveways and sidewalks around schools will quickly transform from relatively quiet areas during the summer to much busier spots as school bells ring starting on Sept. 8 — the day after Labour Day — to mark the start of a new academic year for students in Peel.

items.title: Mississauga to receive up to $401.4 million to support housing and community infrastructure
items.summary: The City’s efforts to make it easier to build new homes, including significant development charge reductions, helped secure the substantial new funding. 4 million in funding to help Mississauga build housing-enabling infrastructure including important new transit projects. Mayor Carolyn Parrish and Members of Council joined Ontario Premier Doug Ford for today’s official announcement alongside Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Jennifer McKelvie, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Housing and Infrastructure and Member of Parliament for Ajax, and Peter Fonseca, Member of Parliament for Mississauga-East Cooksville. The funding, part of the Development Charges Reduction Program, helps municipalities who have reduced development charges invest in the infrastructure they need to support growth. It is part of the broader Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. Mississauga was one of the first cities in Ontario to substantially reduce development charges – by up to 100 per cent – to help get more homes built and make them more affordable. The City has agreed to maintain these reductions until March 31, 2029. The new funding will help support housing-enabling infrastructure including two key transit projects: a new zero-emissions transit maintenance and storage facility and new downtown transit mobility hub. As Canada’s seventh largest city, significant investment in transit infrastructure is critical to support new housing development. These investments, which the City has long advocated for, will help support Mississauga’s growing population and deliver lasting benefits for residents and businesses. The City is planning a new zero-emission transit facility on City-owned land at 7300 West Credit Avenue to support future growth and improve service.

items.title: Lakeview Home's $1.78 Million Over-Asking Sale Tops Mississauga's Market Last Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, a four-bedroom home in Mississauga's Lakeview neighbourhood was the city's most expensive over-asking sale last month, according to a new report from Zoocasa. The outlet reports the home sold for $1,782,777, well above its $1,699,000 list price. INsauga reports the property includes a mudroom with direct garage access, a built-in surround sound system, and a finished basement with a home theatre and wine cellar. According to the outlet, the backyard also features an in-ground pool. INsauga reports the sale was highlighted in Zoocasa's monthly roundup of the Greater Toronto Area's top over-asking home sales, drawing attention to Mississauga's competitive housing market.

items.title: Bromsgrove Road Reopens After Storm Flooding as Mississauga Fares Better Than Other Regions
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga saw flooding and downed trees during this week's severe storms, though the city fared better than several other Ontario regions hit harder by the system. The outlet reports Bromsgrove Road was temporarily closed between Southdown Road and Winston Churchill Boulevard due to flooding before reopening once water levels receded. INsauga reports Credit Valley Conservation has since downgraded its flood warnings for the area. A city spokesperson named McCutcheon told the outlet that Mississauga received a limited number of service requests related to flooding and downed trees compared with other municipalities. According to INsauga, city crews are continuing to assess parks and trails for storm damage in the aftermath of the system.

items.title: Erin Mills Parkway Tower Proposal Scaled Back Under Ontario Land Tribunal Settlement
items.summary: According to INsauga, a massive proposed development at 5100 Erin Mills Parkway has been scaled back under a settlement offer filed with the Ontario Land Tribunal. The outlet reports the original proposal called for nine towers ranging from 20 to 44 storeys with a total of 3,162 units. INsauga reports the revised plan reduces the tallest towers to a maximum of 37 storeys, with building heights across the site now ranging from 20 to 37 storeys depending on location. According to the outlet, only two of the buildings still exceed the 25-storey maximum allowed under the city's Official Plan, down from five buildings in the original proposal. INsauga reports the settlement also relocates a 4,206-square-metre park to the northwest corner of the site.

items.title: Ottawa and Ontario Unveil Development Charges Program Aimed at Mississauga Home Affordability
items.summary: According to a joint announcement covered by Yahoo Finance Canada, the federal and Ontario governments say a new Development Charges Reduction Program is intended to make new homes more affordable in Mississauga and other municipalities. The report says the program is projected to save homebuyers as much as $36,140 per home in construction costs. According to the announcement, buyers of new homes could also receive up to $130,000 in HST relief between April 1, 2026 and March 31, 2027, bringing combined potential savings to as much as $166,140 per home. The funding is tied to the $1.8 billion Build Communities Strong Fund, which the governments say will be distributed over 10 years. According to the report, officials project the program could help unlock 90,000 new homes across the province.
